newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Asian stocks rebound from bout of profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Asian stocks rebound from bout of profit-taking.

text.p: Most Asian stock markets ended higher on Thursday on a variety of local factors with Hong Kong and Tokyo bouncing back from Wednesday's lull and Manila and Wellington steaming ahead for the second straight day.
Profit-takers reappeared in Hong Kong on Thursday but the market shrugged them off, rallying to a strong close led by continued strength in the banking sector, brokers said.
The Hang Seng Index fluctuated throughout the day in a 100-point range, closing up 40.62 points, or 0.33 percent, at 12,436.80.
The index had soared to a new all time high of 12,602.34 on Wednesday, only to end the day down 94.52 points at 12,396.18.
"There is a certain amount of nervousness at this level but few big sellers," said one broker with an international house.

Tokyo stocks also ended a shade higher after wandering narrowly in both negative and positive territory throughout the day. Brokers said investors were waiting for Sunday's elections in the Lower House of parliament before making any moves.
The 225-issue Nikkei average inched up 26.55 points, or 0.12 percent, to 21,423.74.
Manila shares ended on a high note for the second straight day after a sharp fall since the beginning of the month but the run-up failed to convince the market the downtrend had been reversed.
The index rose by 77.49 points, or 2.60 percent, to 3,061.06 points. On Wednesday, it had risen by 56.14 points, or 1.92 percent, to 2,983.57.
Analysts were not convinced the bear spell was over.
"It was too fast. Its a recovery but it has to be tested," said Kevin Khoe, analyst at Sapphire Securities.
The New Zealand share market forged ahead to a fresh 32-month high on Thursday, closing 22.73 points, or 0.98 percent, stronger on heavy volume.
The NZSE-40 Capital index ended at 2,348.71. It has not seen these levels since February 1994.
One analyst said there was a lot of value in the market now that the uncertainty surrounding the October 12 election was reduced by the poor showing of the left-wing Alliance Party.
Australian shares closed weaker on Thursday, the market drifting lower after the Reserve Bank of Australia dampened expectations of a rate cut in its monthly bulletin released on Wednesday.
The key share market indicator, the All Ordinaries index, closed down 11.2 points, or 0.47 percent, at 2,353.8.

Thai stocks gained slightly for the second straight day in a technical rebound. The SET index closed 12.78 points, or 1.39 percent, higher at 929.61 on 3.5 billion baht turnover. The SET-50 index rose 1.18 points to 69.92.
The Jakarta Composite Index rose 3.34 points, or 0.59 percent, to 569.12 points.

Singapore shares closed slightly lower in aimless trade with foreign shares sold down, dealers said. The Straits Times Industrial Index closed down 2.54 points, or 0.12 percent, at 2,068.72 points. ----
At 1130 GMT, the dollar was trading at 112.13/2.25 yen and 1.5389/94 marks.
SIMEX Brent oil futures were traded lower in small volume, continuing a correction seen in London and New York on Wednesday.
December was last traded at $23.88 per barrel, down six cents from the London close on Wednesday of $24.73.
Gold closed slightly lower in Hong Kong on Thursday in lifeless trading, dealers said. Bullion closed at US$380.60/381.10 against New York's Wednesday close of US$380.90/381.40.
